recipes.name: Homestyle Stuffed Peppers
ingredients_raw: 4 medium green bell peppers, tops and seeds removed

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Add peppers and boil until softened, 4 to 5 minutes. Transfer peppers to a colander and run under cold water to cool.
Mix ground beef, cooked rice, bread crumbs, 4 tablespoons Parmesan, onion, egg, garlic powder, salt, and pepper together in a large bowl until well combined.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Spoon beef mixture into peppers.
Place peppers into a baking dish with the stuffing facing up.
Stir tomato sauce and vinegar together in a bowl. Pour tomato sauce mixture over peppers.
Sprinkle remaining 2 tablespoons Parmesan over top.

Bake in the preheated oven, basting peppers with sauce several times, until beef filling is no longer pink in the center, about 1 hour 20 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Homestyle Stuffed Peppers
raw_recipe.description: Old-fashioned stuffed peppers just like mom used to make! Green bell peppers stuffed with beef and rice are smothered in a tangy tomato sauce.

review.reviewBody: Hi I'm Jillian the submitter of the recipe and this is my Mom, Nancy's recipe. I've been making Stuffed Peppers for years and my Mom probably made thousands of these! She taught me how to make them and that's a memory I'll always treasure as she got the recipe from her Mom. Now that she's gone I think of her everytime I make them. She served them with mashed potatoes or sometimes potato salad. I hope you and your family enjoy them as much as I do - it certainly has become one of my husband's favorites! Depending on the size of the green bell peppers, you may not have to boil them for 4-5 minutes, but maybe 3. I use large eggs and 90/10 lean ground beef when preparing these and sometimes add a little more vinegar to the tomato sauce or fresh minced garlic vs. garlic powder (yes, I tweak my own recipes and just for clarification - the beef is not cooked before hand). You can even sub half ground turkey or use all ground turkey for a healthier, lighter version. Enjoy!
My husband and I absolutely loved this recipe! The only thing I changed was we used ground turkey since we don't care for beef. The best stuffed peppers I've eaten, hands down. Mmmmmm

Instead of boiling the peppers, I prepared them and placed them in the microwave for about 10 minutes (more or less depending on the size of the pepper) until they were just slightly softened. I used two pounds of lean ground beef and increased the number of peppers to six. I always use a variety of pepper colors, the yellow are the definitely the sweetest and the green peppers can be bitter. I used three 15 ounce cans of tomato sauce; one can with 2 tablespoons of cider vinegar which I used to cover the bottom of the pan before placing my peppers in it, the other two cans I poured over the peppers before baking. I like to use the sauce, which has the flavor of the peppers and meat juices, over the mashed potatoes and serve them alongside the peppers for a complete meal. A dash of Worcestershire sauce when preparing the meat filling mixture helped give the meat depth of flavor. It was delicious!!

Some of these bad reviews are so rude and I honestly question your cooking abilities! I've made this numerous times and find the recipe to be easy to understand and follow. Every time they turn out wonderful. I've played around with the meats and pepper types and even the sauce sometimes I mix vinegar with spaghetti sauce. Every time they are a huge hit. One of our favs is to add 3/4 c pear cous cous in place of the rice. The recipe is more like a meatloaf consistency but still to die for I personally don't care for the ones that you cook the meat first. This will be one of the recipes I pass down to my children for sure :)

Super great recipe! I've made these peppers a few times and we all love them. I use red and green peppers for a variety and with 1 1/2 lbs beef it easily fills 5-6 peppers. I really like the addition of the vinegar in the tomato sauce. Great with mashed potatoes!

This is a great recipe. My Mother made this as well but I kick it up a notch. Ok, a couple of notches. I add carmelized garlic and onion, celery and diced green chilis and I use 1/2 Italian Sweet Sausage and 1/2 Ground Sirloin for the meat mix. Sometimes all Sausage for even more flavor. My husband would eat these every night and even the 4 picky kids loved them. Sometimes I even use Rice Pilaf mix, rather than white rice. I change it up almost every time, but what reminds me of my Mother's recipe is the Italian Bread Crumbs. Oh, and hers were so nice and neat in the pan; mine are chock-full and spilling all over the pan. The best part for me is the spilled-over insides that are slightly burned and sticking to the pan! Yummers! Super recipe and great memories of your Mom!!! (I just sent hubby to grocery store so I can make these tonight. See what you have done!!!)

We make this dish at least once a month! My fiance and I are gluten free, so just swap out the bread crumbs for corn bread crumbs, and sometimes we mix in some stewed tomato/zucchini/onion. The white vinegar really makes a wonderful difference.

So similar to my mother's recipe. Also served with mashed potatoes. I soften the peppers in the microwave. I mix my meat. Kind of like a meatloaf mix, but do not add the rice to the meat. Fill the peppers with the raw meat mixture, the rice, a couple slices of onion on top of rice, then the pepper top. No cheese. Exactly like my mother’s recipe. The story: my dad hated rice, no idea why, he ate everything and was from a very large family. We never had rice except stuffed peppers. So he got a pepper full of meat. And, hence, the mashed potatoes. My brother hated the pepper and I always got his pepper. When I make it, I am flooded with memories. My husband died recently and I made it for my sister when she visited. She was in tears. It was exactly like our mother's. This is probably. More of a review than you wanted, but this is a very special recipe. Thank you for posting it.

I have been making stuffed peppers for years. The only problem I have run into is that, now people are so health conscious that they have removed most of the fat from the meat. With the loss of fat, so went some of the flavor. So I believe I have solved the problem of ending up with meat stones in the peppers. Most stores make a meatloaf mix, 1/3 veal; 1/3 pork; and 1/3 beef. This adds moisture and flavor. With this 1 alteration this recipe is perfect.

Pretty bland and a lot of trouble. Need to drop old fashioned useless parboiling, up the seasonings and perk up the sauce. I added an envelope of onion soup mix to the filling and made a sweet sour sauce from a can of whole cranberry sauce and a can of tomato sauce. Much better!

Really love filling in this recipe. Just tweaked sauce a bit - used cider vinegar and added a bit of brown sugar. We love some sweet & sour. Also didn't boil or blanch red bell peppers first - they came out tender without being mushy. Great recipe!
I used quinoa instead of rice.

I used this recipe but changed 3 things my grandmother did 1- used pepper scraps in my chopped veg 2- used apple cider vinegar instead of white 3- used pablano peppers in addition to the bell peppers and it brought me back to her kitchen. Very tasty:)”
Great way to use up summer garden peppers! I used ground meatloaf mix and put bacon on top. WOW so delicious!!

I made it with a venison/pork sausage combo, and it was delicious. I left off the cheese, (as some in my family don't love it), and it was honestly so good without it I didn't end up adding it to mine either!

I was very disappointed with this recipe. It sounded so delicious, but it wasn't (at least not to my family). Honestly, it had a funny taste to it. What does that mean? It was the stuffing part that tasted strange. It must be me, because everyone else loved it.
I liked this recipe just put apple cider vinegar instead of white vinegar and added a few shakes of smoked paprika
These were just like the ones my mom made in the '60s and '70s. Delicious!

I used ground turkey mixed it italian turkey sausage ( great flavor) I also added flavored cauliflower rice instead of rice. And I added some roasted tomatoes and peppers to my sauce!! Went well with cabbage. It went over well!! Not one leftover!!

Very good, very tasty, thanks. But way too much filling for the peppers I had. I had six, and had to put leftover into a small glass baking dish to cook it, too. Like mini-meatloaves in an edible dish, less one. Highly recommend, but use big peppers. LOL
